SONA 2017

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
President Zuma will address the nation on Thursday night but the EFF has once again threatened to disrupt proceedings. Journalist covering the event are under the tightest controls ever experienced with accrediation opening and closing in early January with absolutely no substitutions. Access to Spin Street where parliamentarians and guests enter will be off bounds to the media who are limited to two demarcated areas requiring a police escort to move from one to the other. Meanwhile the ANC is hosting a "People's Parliament" on the Grand Parade with the president address broadcast on large screens.

Press Release:


SONA 2017
With security tight around Parliament this week, President Jacob Zuma’s 8th State of the Nation Address gives South Africans a much anticipated road map into 2017. Carte Blanche asks: is the President’s take on simmering hot-button issues from land redistribution to trade policies, free higher education, the scourge of corruption and more, sufficient to restore confidence and economic growth?


Script:


Upsound Malema “ Just kill me”
Script: The State of the Nation address was disrupted for the 3rd year running, but this year it descended into the worst violence and anarchy since 1994. The dramatic increase in security is what had people on edge.
Link: Capetonians have grown accustomed to the ring of steel that is put in place for the state of the nation address but this year it encompasses a far bigger area and it’s policed by 6000 Saps members and more than 400 soldiers
Script: Deploying the army to maintain for law and order is normally only done under exception circumstances. There was a sense that the city was under siege, with Caspirs, police and military on every corner as the security forces prepared for the worst.
As the dignitaries arrived and the usual pomp and ceremony took place safely behind the cordoned off streets, there were violent clashes between the EFF and the ANC
Link " In 1994 this was labelled the peoples’ parliament accessible to all but as Jacob Zuma delivers his 10th State of the Nation address ordinary SA would be forgiven for feeling a sense of alienation both from the president as well as the people mandated to hold them to account
Script: Melanie Verwoerd, political analyst and former ANC parliamentarian and diplomat was in the gallery
Melanie “It does not feel like a peoples’ parliament anymore. The visible police presence the barricades then it goes further by bringing in the military so there is a feeling of being under threat and then the big mistake I think they made was going after the press”
Anthem and salute
Entering parliament upsound
Script: The opposition parties were determined to have their say before the president, with DA chief whip John Steenhuisen attempting to set the tone
Steenhuisen “This is the first sitting since the Esidimeni
Speaker Baleka Mbete “hold on to that point until the debate next week”.
Script: President Zuma however raised it far later in his speech. And as everybody had been warned, EFF leader, Julius Malema stuck to his guns:
Julius Malema: “Mr Zuma has collapsed his own right to address us here, 441 soldiers will never protect you, your problem is not outside, your problem is here, there is no soldiers here (pointing at the ground) rants for a few seconds and says “so we are not going to allow the president to address us” Sits.
Script: Then it was Cope Leader Mosuia Lekota’s turn to lay into the president:
Lekota “the gentleman before you has broken his oath of office, he admitted that, subsequently the court found that he had, he has discharged himself from the oath of office. Madame Speaker, in English, (pointing at Zuma) he is called a scoundrel, in our mother tongue lemele mele.“
Baleka Mbete “Freedom of expression is being abused by yourselves
Melanie “ Tthe EFF went in there it was clearly the agenda they didn’t want to stay they wanted to be thrown out and they were going to do it with maximum amount of violence because it makes for the best TV and the best TV shots. But as usual the speaker and the NCOP less so the NCOP chair struggled to keep order and made mistakes with the minute of silence that they denied and that just aggravates the situation but there is a bigger problem and that is the respect for the president and the institution has gone
Script: Political analyst and author Ralph Mathekga says the EFF strategy of disruption needs re thinking
Ralph” The reason why what the EFF has been doing has been able to gain traction since they have come to parliament is because the ANC have given them material for that, and I think there is some lack of stategy with what they aim to achieve, there is no way they had realistically thought Jacob Zuma would stop giving the State of the Nation because they believe so
Mmusi Maimane “we saw earlier on today army members even here on the precinct. The fact of the matter is that the constitution has been violated, which is something even PW Botha would have been proud of. The leader of the ANC who is here has violated the constitution.
Script: This continued for over an hour
“Honourable Malema, we will assist you to leave.”
Script: Then all hell broke loose as the Parliamentary Protection Unit moved in. The EFF were aggressively removed. Punches were thrown and rocks, hard hats and bottles of water were used as weapons
Malema: “We won’t be intimidated by soldiers by police by criminals who are hell bent at defending a constitutional delinquent a man who is prepared to violate the constitution. They are ready to throw out the members who break the rules of parliament but prepared to defend a man who broke his oath of office.
President: Trying again to speak
Links “The dust is starting to settle on what were some very ugly scenes in the national assembly including we understand the use of pepper spray in the chamber and on the night of many firsts perhaps the most sinister is that for the first time at the opening of parliament we have seen riot police in the precinct
Steenhuisen: “Madam House Chair, Madam Speaker, no democracy should have to witness what we are witnessing in this house. This man has broken South Africa, and you are breaking parliament.”
Script: The DA chose to leave rather than be forcibly removed
Musi “There was no ways that this government would use teargas on innocent people. Who would believe we could arrive at that day so when a decisions like that is taken we have to leave we have no choice because what’s next you say anything in parliament who knows what danger you could putting yourself in against the constitution of the republic it violates the very essence of what democracy is about.
Script: The walk out sparked fresh clashes on the streets as people tried to get closer to parliament to either support the EFF or the president with the police ensuring they kept the two sides apart
Ralph “ As long as we don’t have a harsh judgement from society of that behaviour both of the President Jacob Zuma and the reaction of the EFF that space will continue to exist and all it takes is for another political party to come to pursue this disruptive politics
Script: ANC Secretary General Gwede Matashe expressed his frustration
Gwede “If I was a the speaker I would not have allowed that debate to go for an hour I would have finished it in 20 minutes
Script: With both major opposition parties missing, President Jacob Zuma finally began to address the nation on a broad range of issue
President “Today we are starting a new chapter of radical economic transformation we are saying we should move beyond words to practical programs
Script: Dean of UCT’s Graduate School of Business Mills Soko says the ANC promised this in 2014
Soko. One of the problems we have in SA is that the Government doesn’t have a clear economic policy even the announcement of this Radical Economic Transformation Program, we need a plan we need to target and that is not coming through and what is coming through is that it is a lot of soundbites and I am not sure if there is genuine commitment to this program or whether it has something to do with politicking ahead of the 2019
Ralph” Well I think the intention of this radical economic transformation is not necessarly to effect some substantive shift in the economic trajectory. I think the intention actually is for the ANC to reclaim the space in the public discourse that is the reason why there is no clarity as to what does radical economic transformation mean
Zuma “ It is difficult to achieve if not impossible to achieve true reconciliation until the land question is resolved. Only 8 million hectares of arable land have been transferred to black people which is only 8.2 % of the 82 million hectares of arable land in SA
Soko The performance of the government in relation to that issue has been extremely appalling. There was a study that was published recently which showed that 9 out of 10 of black farmers that were given land over the past years those have failed so it is not just about parcelling out land, it is about providing the necessary programs to enable the emerging farmer to succeed.
Ralph “Had we maybe wanted to pursue this land issue we should we should have allocating a large sum of money to that. Some people have said 60 billion which is the equivalent of what we spend on arms.
Script: And as South Africa struggles to keep its international credit ratings from being rendered “junk”, the world is watching – Sona 2017 did us few favours.
Melanie “We are playing into the worst foreign stereotypes that every foreign investor and country will have about SA and as much as we want radical economic transformation in this country and our economy to keep growing and the only way we can do that is for us to we get foreign investment
Soko” What is required is leadership, maturity, compromise, that is not happening currently but I will also emphasise the importance of leadership taking control and we work towards the broader good of SA rather than the factional interests that characterise inter party relations currently.
